stat_contract.open_issues: total_count of `repo:PipFoweraker/pdoom1 is:issue is:open`. Pull requests are EXCLUDED by is:issue. This is not the same number as GitHub's repository `open_issues_count`, which includes them.
stat_contract.open_pull_requests: total_count of `... is:pr is:open`. A proposed change waiting to go in.
stat_contract.open_issues_without_label: total_count of `... is:issue is:open no:label`. Labels are hand-applied, so this is the count of open issues nobody has categorised. Every label count is a FLOOR, not a total, and this number is how far off the floor could be.
stat_contract.label_counts: total_count of `... is:issue is:open label:<name>` for each label named in `counts`. An issue carrying two of these labels is counted under both; the label counts therefore do NOT sum to open_issues and must never be presented as a partition.
stat_contract.null_means: UNKNOWN -- the query did not come back on this run. It does not mean zero, and nothing downstream may render it as a number.
stat_contract.no_floor: There is no minimum and no fallback. A count that could not be measured is null; the previous run's value is never carried forward under a new as_of.

recent_window.predicate: GitHub's /issues?state=open endpoint, which returns PULL REQUESTS alongside issues. `pull_requests_in_window` says how many of the entries in `issues` are actually pull requests; an entry is one when it carries a `pull_request` key.
recent_window.is_not: a complete list. It is the most recently touched fifteen. Absence from it proves nothing -- see content/campaigns/*.json, which already records that trap.

_comment: issues is a SAMPLE -- the `sample_requested` most recently updated open issues, pull requests removed. total_open_issues is the real count from /search/issues and may be null, which means UNKNOWN and must never render as zero. Bodies are deliberately absent: nothing renders them and they are third-party text on a public host.
